column2: A suitably experienced expert can provide professional career evidence; rumors, ignorance and account selling do not establish relevant expertise.
Theme/time/participants are planning necessities; attendees' passwords, other classes' secret scores and browser histories are unnecessary private data.
Career knowledge/skills help compare requirements with learning plans; proprietary credentials/client records/unconsented private data do not belong in the report.
The institution's official curriculum is a suitable primary source; unattributed comments, address-free ads and altered images are weaker evidence. Publication date still matters.
Task allocation clarifies responsibility and schedule; it does not automatically validate all sources or remove collaboration/content requirements.
Preannounced criteria support fair content/presentation/discussion assessment; clothing cost, friendship and computer price are irrelevant biases.
Citing source and collection date enables checks for relevance/currency; collecting passwords or all applicant records is neither needed nor justified.
A personal study plan links interests, ability and career needs; irrevocable career pledges, credentials and copied income rumors are unsuitable outcomes.

Compare years and use the applicable official current notice, not sum/max/popularity. Clarify both notices are official and concern the same institution so mere recency of an untrusted website is not recommended.
Q&A clarifies uncertainty and supports checking/extension; it does not replace preparation, suppress difference or license private disclosures.
Good visuals do not compensate for missing professional content or validate sources/decisions. Distinct assessment dimensions are correctly explained.
True: self-assessment identifies gaps relative to professional requirements, matching Mai's stated weaknesses.
True: studying English and practicing networks directly addresses the specified gaps; a realistic plan rather than a job guarantee.
False: an unverified pay-now employment promise needs verification rather than immediate payment.
False: interest motivates but does not replace necessary knowledge/skills.
VGA carries analog video; not Bluetooth pairing, audio-only content or a power-supply channel. Correct textbook legacy-interface scope.
Discovery and appropriate pairing confirmation are usual Bluetooth setup steps; DNS, inserting network cables into all USB ports and converting images are unrelated.
Duplicate mirrors the principal display; Extend adds workspace. Display-resolution differences do not alter the conceptual mirror mode.
Extend expands desktop workspace; it does not duplicate stored files, increase physical RAM or convert HTML files.
Windows+P opens projection/display modes in the explicitly scoped Windows lesson; it is not a universal shortcut across operating systems.
Wi-Fi/other wireless protocols commonly link smart-home devices; paper notes, printed tables and labels are not communication protocols. Does not exclude wired smart homes.
A compatible smart-home app can monitor/control devices, not physically replace hardware, generate energy or repair all sensors.
Both peers need enabled Bluetooth support and suitable range; equal screen size/storage/Windows username is unnecessary. Necessary conditions, not an exhaustive sufficiency claim.

Extend permits separate working regions. Correct inaccurate distractor descriptions: Second screen only disables the main display, not the entire computer; make all mode alternatives factually named but unsuitable to two distinct views.
Remote Internet-platform control ordinarily requires the home hub/device and phone to be connected; local Bluetooth differs in range. Qualified 'usually' avoids denying other remote channels.
Matching pairing identity/code helps avoid the wrong partner; it does not alter processor speed, file types or memory capacity.
Correct remedy is selecting the matching input, but stem did not identify HDMI. Specify the HDMI cable explicitly; televisions can also use other input standards.
Bluetooth is the nearby wireless use in this book, unlike intercontinental fiber/satellite or an HTML-only interface; no fixed universal range is asserted.
PC screen only uses the main PC display; second-only/mirror/extended modes are distinct choices.
True: the described supported app can manage names, schedules and state; not a promise every vendor exposes identical controls.
True: power, networking and pairing are relevant first checks before attributing failure to hardware.
False: disconnecting the home's Internet is not a remedy for the specified Internet-platform remote control.
False: scheduling switching does not generate electrical energy; the controlled load still needs power.
Logo supports institutional/brand recognition; it does not store visitor credentials or modify IP/memory. Common placement is qualified.
Favicon appears on browser tabs and related UI, not physical keyboards, modem labels or display cables.
Navigation links move among sections/pages; not physical brightness, global administrator access or memory processing speed.
Purpose and intended audience precede content/design decisions; random images, publishing passwords and deletion are not appropriate first planning steps.
Colors/fonts/images are visual design choices; power/network/timetable parameters are different categories.
Contact/copyright/links are ordinary footer information; secrets and hardware components are not appropriate public footer content.
Google Sites is the book's visual website builder; hardware replacement/electrical measurement/HDMI generation are unrelated.
Text/images/multimedia are website source materials, subject to relevance/rights/trust; credentials or physical electrical/computer parts are not the requested content assets.
Excessive inconsistent color/type can reduce readability; simplifying/cohering design is appropriate, not claiming visuals replace substance.
A sitemap clarifies hierarchy and navigation; it does not generate assets, buy domains or automatically verify evidence.
Image rights should be considered during collection, not only after complaints; public availability is not blanket permission.
False: more typefaces plus foreground/background equality reduces readability rather than improving it.
False: favicon is an identifying image, not an authentication password.
True: a consistent palette and limited appropriate fonts address the specific visual inconsistency.
True: the body organizes primary topical content into comprehensible regions; 'usually' appropriately avoids rigid universal layout requirements.
The book's Sites draft is managed in the user's Google Drive, not monitor ROM/router card/printer. Add explicit textbook-version scope; do not confuse editor artifact with published web hosting.
Header type changes the top-region layout (cover/banner/title-only), not SQL keys, network protocols or drivers. UI labels are textbook-version examples.
Preview checks rendered layouts before publication; it neither erases content nor changes accounts/shares passwords. Official Sites help confirms device-layout preview.
Publish makes a site version available at its URL subject to viewer permissions; not an automatic permission grant to the world. Official publish/share guidance agrees.
Brand Images contains logo/favicon controls in the book and current official help; unrelated network/password/disk settings do not.
A simple legible small icon works as favicon; long tiny text, blur and embedded passwords do not. Square is a recommendation, not a universal file-format mandate.
Header Change image selects its background; deleting accounts/changing passwords/disconnecting networks cannot implement that design change.
Top or side navigation are the described Sites options and current official modes; not hardware/credential storage locations. Availability may depend on page/theme context.
Improve foreground/background contrast to cure white-on-bright text; removing navigation or denying viewers does not address readability.
A draft in the editor is not necessarily published or visible to all; publish status and viewer permissions must be checked. Never share the editor's password.
Stored project name and displayed title can differ in Sites; no image-background restriction or mandatory account-name equality exists.
False: Preview is not an editor-permission grant, as official preview/share documentation distinguishes.
False: viewer-only access does not need Drive ownership; ownership is excessive and changes control.
True: both logo and favicon contribute identity without replacing substantive page content.
True: testing as the intended viewer catches access restrictions; use the actual target role rather than assuming editor access proves public access.
